fields.meta_title: Approval Workflow: Build and Automate Approvals | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an approval workflow from a prompt: request form, multi-level routing, Slack and email alerts, and an audit log you own. Free to start.
fields.hero_description: Build an approval workflow that sends every request to the right approver and keeps each decision in a log you own.
fields.features_subheading: Purchase orders, invoices, contracts, and expenses. Emergent builds the request form, routing, alerts, and audit database behind them.
fields.feature_1:
Request form generated with the workflow

The intake form is built with the approval workflow, not bolted on after. Every field maps to a routing rule, and a policy change updates the form and the routing together.
fields.feature_2:
Sequential, parallel, or multi-level routing

One approver at a time, several in parallel, tiers by amount, or branches by department. Describe a multi-level approval rule in one sentence and it becomes the routing logic.
fields.feature_3:
Approve from Slack, Teams, or email

Every approver gets the request details and a one-click approve or reject in the channel they already use. The decision writes back to the workflow, with no separate portal.
fields.feature_4:
Escalation timers and fallback approvers

When an approver hasn't acted in the time you set, send a reminder, escalate to their manager, or hand it to a fallback approver. Put the timing in the prompt and every step uses it.
fields.feature_5:
An audit trail in a database you own

Every decision, reminder, and escalation lands in a table with requester, approver, amount, reason, and time to approve. Finance and audit query it directly, with no PDF exports.
fields.feature_6:
Full code export

The whole app, intake form and decision log included, exports to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Nothing stays locked in a per-seat tool or a proprietary workflow canvas.

fields.usecase_heading: Approval Workflows Built From One Prompt
fields.tab_content_1:
Purchase requests routed by dollar amount

Anything under $500 goes to the requester's manager, requests up to $5,000 go to the department head, and larger ones add the CFO. Nina Park's $4,800 order for 12 design licenses skips the manager and lands in #approvals for Priya Shah. Once she approves, the bill is created in Xero.
fields.tab_content_2:
Read the invoice, match the PO, then route it

Each invoice that arrives by email or upload is read by an AI step that pulls out the vendor, PO reference, total, and due date. Pinemoor Supply Co. sends INV-7731 for $2,340.00. It matches PO-2231, and anything over $1,000 goes to finance before the bill syncs to Xero.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three reviewers at once, with a nudge after two days

Legal, finance, and the executive sponsor get the master services agreement at once. Lena Grant in legal moves payment terms to 30 days, and finance signs off. David Kim, the sponsor, has gone two days without a reply, and a reminder reaches him Thursday at 9:00 AM. Signing opens once all three approve.
fields.tab_content_4:
A $180 dinner checked against policy and budget

Snap the receipt on a phone, pick the category and project, and submit. This client dinner for project Atlas sits under the $250 meal limit and inside the $4,000 October budget. Marcus Lee approves it in 12 minutes and it joins the accounting export queue. Anything over policy goes to finance review instead.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Approval Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set the rules of an approval workflow and test it on one team, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose how you will build it
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide where your approvals will live before you build anything. In email and spreadsheets, the request and the decision sit in different places, and nothing chases a quiet approver. Emergent generates the form, the routing, and the audit log in one build, with every approver included.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Define the trigger and the request
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name what starts the approval: a submitted form, an uploaded invoice, an inbound email, or a deal change in HubSpot. The trigger decides the request fields, such as amount, vendor, department, category, and the documents a reviewer needs to decide without asking.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write who approves what, and in what order: under $500 to the manager, $500 to $5,000 to the department head, above that to the CFO, with legal in parallel for contracts. Written as plain sentences, the matrix becomes the routing logic.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide what happens when an approver goes quiet: a reminder after one business day, escalation to their manager after two, and a fallback approver when someone is out of office. These timings decide your cycle time more than any other rule.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an approval workflow for my team's purchase requests.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put approve and reject where approvers already work: Slack, Microsoft Teams, or email, with the full request context in the message. Each click is stored against the request, and nobody has to log in to a separate portal to clear a queue.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Decide what the audit log records
fields.howto_step_6_des: Record the requester, approver chain, amount, decision, reason, and time to approve for every request. On Emergent the log is a database table you own. A dashboard on top of it shows cycle time by approver, and auditors read the same rows.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Pilot with one team, then roll out
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn it on for one team, run real requests through it for two weeks, and read time to approve from the audit log. Tighten the rules and timings by prompting, then roll it out to the next department, with every version kept in exportable code.
